_real_world.variant_scope: F135-PW-100 CTOL-lineage engine as fitted to the F-35C carrier variant (optional CVW-8 branch, count 0 in the 2025-26 deployment)
public_equipment: F135-PW-100, 28,000 lbf military / 43,000 lbf afterburning thrust class (Pratt & Whitney official specification)

_provenance.modeling_note: F-35C is the optional CVW-8 branch (count 0 in the 2025-26 baseline per the OOB page). Pratt & Whitney's public F135 specification sheet lists F135-PW-100 (CTOL/F-35A) and F135-PW-400 (carrier variant/F-35C) as producing 'almost identical results'; this record uses the same published thrust figures for both, matching the source's own statement that the CV engine differs mainly in corrosion-resistant materials, not performance.

engine.mil_thrust_n.note: 28,000 lbf military (Intermediate) thrust class per Pratt & Whitney F135 official spec sheet; 28000 x 4.4482 = 124549.6 N

engine.ab_thrust_n.note: 43,000 lbf maximum (afterburning) thrust class per Pratt & Whitney official spec sheet; 43000 x 4.4482 = 191272.6 N

engine.sfc_mil.note: no public SFC found for F135; proxy engineering_estimate patterned on repo F110-GE-129 (aircraft/modules/engines/f110_ge_129.json), a comparable-generation high-bypass-for-fighter afterburning turbofan

engine.sfc_ab.note: same proxy reasoning as sfc_mil, from repo F110-GE-129

engine.bypass_ratio.note: 0.57 engineering_estimate; publicly reported F135 bypass ratio figures are inconsistent/unconfirmed in open sources, using a mid-range low-bypass fighter turbofan estimate consistent with F119 lineage, not a sourced figure
